## Safe server updates
- **Debian / Ubuntu script:** running it again updates without losing anything. Before every update it now stops the server and saves a copy of the database in `/var/lib/streyn/backups` (the last 5 are kept)
- **Lost data comes back:** if the server starts empty but an older data folder (for example `/var/lib/musik` from before the rename) still has a database, the script takes it over again. The empty one is kept as a backup
- **An old Musik service** that still runs next to Streyn is switched off, so it can't block the port
- **Update button in the app** also saves a database copy before the new version starts

## Updates in the app
- **Bar at the top** when the app or the server is behind the newest version, with an Update button. Close it with the x, it comes back with the next release
- **Server update with live output:** the update shows what the server does, line by line, like a terminal (release lookup, backup, download, restart)
- Normal users can only update their app; the server stays with admins

## Invite links
- **Settings → Users → Invite link:** makes a link for a new person. They open it, pick a name and a password and get a normal account
- Each link works once and for 7 days

## Proxmox
- **Notes follow the version:** the container notes (Summary → Notes) now update by themselves within 5 minutes after every update, also after updates from the app. Run the Proxmox script once to switch this on

## Website
- **Windows server:** the Windows tab has a command that always downloads the newest server, and a direct download that shows the current version

## Downloads
- Releases only carry the Streyn files now (Streyn.apk, Streyn.exe, Streyn.AppImage, streyn-server-*). The old Musik.* copies are gone. Apps older than 1.14 need to be installed fresh once from musik.labtoso.de
- Every release has a description of what changed

## Install
- **Update server:** Settings → Updates → Update now (or run the Proxmox script)
- **Android:** Settings → Updates → Update now
- **Windows:** Settings → Updates, or run the new installer
- **Linux:** Settings → Updates
